source: v3-flat fixup (Devon 2026-11-07 rules): restores concern facts the v3 batches dropped (rBST, dyes, glyphosate, seed oils, egg safety), the G2/G3 glosses, two allowlisted or pointer sentences tests pin verbatim, and breaks two meat-section repeated phrases and one tier_note restatement. Every quote is a verbatim substring of the same card before the run.

replace.from: “100% grass-fed” plain whole-milk yogurt with the Certified Grassfed seal, “cream-top” or “non-homogenized”.
replace.text: “100% grass-fed” plain whole-milk yogurt with the Certified Grassfed seal.

remove: A short list is the sign: milk and cultures.
No added vitamins and no thickeners. Thickeners do the job straining does, for less.

add.text: Organic or “rBST free”: no rBST, a synthetic growth hormone, in the herd.
add.quote: rBST is a synthetic growth hormone used in dairy cows

add.text: A short list is the sign: milk and cultures. No added color, dyes, thickeners or vitamins. Thickeners do the job straining does, for less.
add.quote: A short list is the sign: milk and cultures

replace.from: Plain over flavored and fruit-on-the-bottom tubs, where the added sugar is.
replace.text: 100% grass-fed on the tub means the cows ate grass and hay, never grain.
replace.quote: 100% grass-fed on the tub means the cows ate grass and hay, never grain.

replace.from: Greek and skyr are strained: thicker, with less whey. Whole-milk versions are more filling and less tinkered with than fat-free.
replace.text: Greek and skyr are strained: thicker, with less whey.
replace.quote: Greek and skyr are strained: thicker, with less whey.

replace.from: Can’t find 100% grass-fed: plain organic whole-milk yogurt.
replace.text: Can’t find 100% grass-fed: plain organic whole-milk yogurt. Whole-milk versions are more filling and less tinkered with than fat-free.
replace.quote: Whole-milk versions are more filling and less tinkered with than fat-free.

remove: Farm stands and farmers markets for soy-free eggs.
The farm named on the carton.

add.text: Farm stands, farmers markets or the farm named on the carton, for soy-free eggs.
Open the carton and check for cracks and leaks before it goes in the cart.
add.quote: Open the carton and check for cracks and leaks before it goes in the cart.

remove: Time outdoors in print, beyond “cage-free” or “vegetarian-fed”.

add.text: “Pasture-raised” means time outdoors on pasture, audited only with a certifier’s seal.
add.quote: “Pasture-raised” means time outdoors on pasture, audited only with a certifier’s seal.

add.text: Time outdoors in print, beyond “cage-free” or “vegetarian-fed”.

replace.text: Organic, since conventional oats may be sprayed with glyphosate before harvest.
replace.quote: Conventional oats may be sprayed with glyphosate

replace.from: ‘Whole’ in the first ingredient; a loaf called just ‘wheat’ may be white flour.
replace.text: Whole wheat in the first ingredient; a loaf called just ‘wheat’ may be white flour.
replace.quote: a loaf called just ‘wheat’ may be white flour

replace.from: A 100% Whole Grain Stamp over 50%+ or Basic.
replace.text: A 100% Whole Grain Stamp, the top of its three tiers.
replace.quote: Check the Whole Grain Stamp: 100%, 50%+ and Basic

replace.from: “Raw” and “unfiltered”, with the pollen left in: cloudy, not clear.
replace.text: Honey labeled “raw” and “unfiltered”, with the pollen left in: cloudy, not clear.
replace.quote: “raw” and “unfiltered”, with the pollen left in

replace.from: The qualifier after “Uncured”, which can still mean celery-based curing.
replace.text: “Uncured” can still mean celery-based curing; read the qualifier.
replace.quote: “Uncured” can still mean celery-based curing; read the qualifier.

replace.text: Olives in brine over lye-treated olives.

add.text: Organic, since conventional wheat may be sprayed with glyphosate.
add.quote: conventional wheat may be sprayed with glyphosate

add.text: No sunflower, safflower, canola, soybean, corn or cottonseed oil.
add.quote: sunflower, safflower, canola, soybean, corn, cottonseed

add.text: Organic, since conventional chickpeas may get glyphosate before harvest.

replace.text: Organic beans, dried or canned, since conventional pulses may get glyphosate.

add.text: No Red 40, Yellow 5, Yellow 6 or Blue 1 dyes; a “Lake” dye still counts.

replace.from: Every curing substance named on the ingredients list.
replace.text: Read the ingredients list; every curing substance has to be named there.
replace.quote: Read the ingredients list; every curing substance has to be named there.

replace.text: Farmed mussels, oysters and clams, which filter their food from the water.
replace.quote: they filter their food from the water
